t: Which of the following correctly pairs the engineering policy with the phase of an asset's life it protects?
o: CAR – operation of a completed bridge
MBD – transit of machinery from the manufacturer
EAR – erection and testing of plant before commissioning
CECR – construction of a dam
e: EAR covers storage, erection and testing; CAR covers construction, CECR completed structures and MBD operating machinery.

t: Insurance of engineering risks in India is regulated primarily by:
o: The Reserve Bank of India
The Bureau of Indian Standards
The Tariff Advisory Committee, which still fixes engineering rates
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India under the Insurance Act, 1938 and the IRDA Act, 1999
e: IRDAI regulates insurers, products and policyholder protection; the TAC's rate-fixing role ended with detariffing in 2007.

t: Which of the following is a common feature of all engineering material damage policies?
o: They cover only fire and allied perils
They indemnify sudden and unforeseen physical loss and exclude gradual causes such as wear, tear and corrosion
They are issued without any excess
They cover consequential loss automatically
e: Engineering covers respond to accidental, sudden events; gradual deterioration, consequential loss and claims below the excess are excluded.

t: Which of the following parties can be named as insured under a CAR policy?
o: Only the principal, never the contractor
The contractor alone, in all cases
Only the financing bank
The principal, the contractor and the sub-contractors in respect of their respective interests
e: CAR is usually issued in the joint names of all parties with an insurable interest in the works, with the financier's interest noted where required.

t: Under CAR Section I, property damaged by an insured peril is indemnified on the basis of:
o: Cost of repair or replacement to restore it to its condition immediately before the loss, less salvage
Market value of the damaged materials
Contract profit lost by the contractor
Original cost plus 10% profit
e: CAR pays the cost of reinstating the damaged works; profit, betterment and improvements are not payable.

t: Under CAR, which of the following losses is covered in respect of construction plant on site?
o: Only if the value of plant is declared and included under a specific section/extension of the policy
Automatically, as part of the contract works
Never, since plant is a CPM subject
Only for plant belonging to the principal
e: Contractor's plant can be covered under CAR by declaration at a separate rate; otherwise it must be insured under a CPM policy.

t: A CAR policy with a sum insured of ₹120 crore carries the condition of average. At the time of a flood loss of ₹24 lakh, the completed value of the works is found to be ₹150 crore. The excess for AOG perils is 10% of the claim. The amount payable is:
A CAR policy carries an excess of 5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹25,000 for normal perils. Formwork collapses and the assessed loss is ₹3,60,000. The amount payable is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). 5% of ₹3,60,000 is ₹18,000, which is below the minimum of ₹25,000, so the excess deducted is ₹25,000 and ₹3,35,000 is payable.

t: Which of the following is normally subject to a higher excess under a CAR policy?
o: Damage by fire
Damage by collision of site vehicles
Damage by earthquake, flood, storm and landslide (AOG perils)
Theft of materials
e: AOG perils attract a higher excess because of their catastrophic and widespread nature.

t: A CAR policy on a tunnelling project includes a 'dewatering' exposure. Which statement is correct?
o: Cost of dewatering is covered automatically under Section I
Dewatering is excluded under all circumstances
Dewatering costs are covered only where the extension is purchased and are usually sub-limited
Dewatering is a Section II liability
e: Expenses for pumping out water after an insured event (and the risk of failure of dewatering) are specifically underwritten with limits because of the high exposure in tunnels and basements.

t: Which of the following statements regarding the EAR policy excess is correct?
o: There is no excess under EAR
The excess during the testing period is generally higher than for the erection period
The excess applies only to third-party claims
The excess is fixed at ₹1,000 for all claims
e: Testing is the most hazardous phase and attracts a higher excess, as do AOG perils.

t: Under an EAR policy for an imported plant, 'additional customs duty' extension covers:
o: Customs duty refunded by the Government
Anti-dumping duty
Duty on the entire plant
Extra duty payable on import of replacement parts following an insured loss, over and above the duty included in the sum insured
e: Replacement parts imported after a loss attract fresh duty; the extension covers this additional cost up to a limit.

t: For an EAR proposal of a chemical plant, the underwriter asks for a bar chart. The principal reason is to:
o: Verify the contractor's licence
Determine the build-up of sum insured over time and the timing of the testing period
Check the number of workers
Fix the GST rate
e: The schedule shows when value at risk peaks and when testing — the most hazardous phase — will occur.

t: An EAR policy for a refinery unit with sum insured ₹600 crore is written with a 4-week testing period. Hot testing eventually takes 10 weeks. The insured should:
o: Do nothing, as testing is covered until completion
Obtain an extension of the testing period at additional premium before the original period expires
Buy an MBD policy for the testing period
Cancel the EAR policy and buy a fire policy
e: Testing beyond the included period must be extended with the insurer's agreement; otherwise damage during the extended testing is uninsured.

t: Which of the following would an EAR insurer regard as a 'second-hand' item for the purpose of the testing exclusion?
o: A new machine imported in CKD condition
A machine purchased new but stored for three months before erection
A used machine relocated from another plant of the insured
A machine manufactured in India under licence
e: Previously used/relocated machinery is second-hand; its testing is excluded because latent defects are likely to surface.

t: Under an EAR policy, damage to the insured plant resulting from an error during cold testing (no-load trial) is:
o: Excluded as testing is never covered
Covered only for imported machinery
Covered, cold and hot testing both being within the testing period cover
Covered only if the manufacturer supervised the test
e: Both cold (no-load) and hot (load) testing fall within the EAR testing period, subject to the testing excess.

t: A compressor insured under MBD for ₹8 lakh suffers a total loss. Its new replacement value at the time of loss is ₹10 lakh and depreciation works out to 30%. Ignoring excess and salvage, the insurer pays:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Total loss is settled at actual value (₹10 lakh less 30% = ₹7 lakh); as the sum insured is only 80% of the replacement value, average reduces this to ₹5,60,000.

t: A CPM policy covers which of the following perils?
o: Mechanical breakdown of the engine
Normal depreciation
Wear and tear of tracks
Fire, collision, overturning, flood, earthquake, theft and malicious damage to the plant at site
e: CPM is an all-risks cover for external accidents; breakdown, wear and depreciation are excluded.

t: Under CPM, damage to replaceable parts such as ropes, belts, chains, tyres and batteries is:
o: Always covered in full
Excluded unless the damage is caused by the same accident that damages the machine as a whole
Covered at 50%
Covered only after 12 months
e: Replaceable parts are excluded on their own, but are paid for when they are damaged along with other parts in an insured accident.

t: A contractor's excavator worth ₹80 lakh (replacement value) is insured under CPM for ₹50 lakh. It overturns and the repair cost is ₹8 lakh. Ignoring excess, the insurer pays:
e: Average applies: ₹8 lakh × 50/80 = ₹5,00,000, because the sum insured is only 62.5% of the replacement value.

t: Which of the following best explains why fire, lightning, explosion and flood are excluded under MBD?
o: They never damage machinery
They are covered under the CPM policy
They are uninsurable in India
They are insurable under the Standard Fire and Special Perils policy and MBD avoids duplication of cover
e: MBD complements the fire policy by covering internal causes; the fire perils are left to the fire policy to avoid overlap.

t: Under MBD, loss due to 'centrifugal force' is best illustrated by:
o: Theft of a motor
Corrosion of a pipeline
Fire in a cable gallery
Bursting of a flywheel or grinding wheel from over-speed
e: Tearing apart by centrifugal force (e.g. over-speeding rotors or flywheels) is a classic mechanical breakdown peril.

t: Which of the following conditions commonly applies to an MBD policy?
o: The insured must keep the machinery in good working order and permit inspection by the insurer's engineers
The insured must replace all machinery every five years
The insurer will pay for routine servicing
The policy is cancelled if a machine is idle for a day
e: Maintenance and inspection conditions are central to MBD underwriting; idle machinery remains covered while at rest.

t: A sugar mill's cane crusher insured under MBD (sum insured ₹2 crore) suffers damage to its rollers; repair cost ₹12 lakh includes ₹1.5 lakh for replacing the roller linings which were worn and due for replacement. Excess is 1% of sum insured. Amount payable:
e: Worn parts due for replacement are not payable: ₹12 lakh − ₹1.5 lakh = ₹10.5 lakh; less excess ₹2 lakh = ₹8,50,000.

t: After a partial loss is paid under MBD, the sum insured on the affected machine:
o: Is automatically reduced by the claim amount for the rest of the policy period unless reinstated by payment of pro-rata premium
Is doubled
Is cancelled
Remains unchanged without any premium
e: Engineering policies provide for reinstatement of the sum insured after a loss on payment of pro-rata additional premium, failing which the sum insured stands reduced.

t: Which of the following is NOT a standard MBD exclusion?
o: Loss due to wilful act or gross negligence of the insured
Loss due to cavitation, erosion or rust
Loss due to short circuit
Loss due to experiments or tests involving abnormal stress
e: Short circuit is an insured peril; wilful acts, gradual causes and experiments are excluded.

t: Which of the following must usually be produced by the insured for a boiler to be accepted under BPP?
o: An ISO 9001 certificate
A fire NOC from the municipality
A pollution control board certificate
A valid certificate of inspection under the Boilers Act, 1923
e: Statutory inspection certificates evidence that the boiler is in a fit condition and are a basic underwriting requirement.

t: A BPP policy issued to a textile mill covers the boiler and an air receiver with a combined sum insured of ₹50 lakh and a surrounding property limit of ₹20 lakh. An explosion destroys the boiler (actual value ₹30 lakh, repair not possible) and damages the boiler house costing ₹25 lakh to repair. Ignoring excess and salvage, total payable:
e: Boiler: ₹30 lakh (actual value); surrounding property limited to ₹20 lakh of the ₹25 lakh; total ₹50,00,000.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: An MLOP policy is issued with annual gross profit of ₹1.2 crore but the actual annual gross profit is ₹1.6 crore. A breakdown causes a loss of gross profit of ₹20 lakh after time excess. The amount payable is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Average applies: ₹20 lakh × 1.2/1.6 = ₹15,00,000; the insured bears the balance for underinsurance.

t: Which of the following is a standard EEI exclusion?
o: Damage due to failure of the public electricity supply causing a surge in the equipment
Costs incurred for rectification of functional failures not caused by physical damage
Damage caused by water leakage from the roof
Theft by forcible entry
e: Functional failure without physical damage is a maintenance matter; surge, water damage and burglary are insured perils.

t: Under Section III of an EEI policy, the insured must declare:
o: The indemnity period and the daily or monthly amount of extra cost for substitute facilities
The number of employees
The depreciation rate of the equipment
The fire policy number
e: ICOW is rated on the agreed daily/monthly amount and indemnity period, with a time excess.

t: An EEI proposal is received for computers that are 12 years old. The appropriate underwriting action is:
o: Accept at standard rate
Accept at half the standard rate
Accept with free data media cover
Decline or accept with suitable loading/higher excess after considering age, maintenance contract and condition
e: Age and maintenance are key EEI rating factors; old equipment is prone to failures and spares may be unavailable.

t: An EEI policy on a hospital's diagnostic equipment has Sections I and II. After a short circuit damages the equipment, the hospital loses patient scan records stored on an external drive which was physically damaged in the same event. Which sections respond?
o: Section I only
Section II only
Section I for the equipment and Section II for the damaged data media and reconstruction of data
Neither section
e: Section I pays for the equipment; Section II pays for the physically damaged external media and data reconstruction.

t: Which of the following is a standard condition for DOS cover?
o: The cold storage must be inspected and the machinery maintained in good condition, with stock and temperature records kept
The stock must be owned by the insurer
Stock must be insured under a fire policy with the same insurer
The cold storage must be less than 3 years old
e: Temperature logs and stock registers are essential for assessing a DOS claim and the plant must be maintained to the insurer's satisfaction.

t: Under DOS, the premium rate typically depends on:
o: The age of the owner
The distance from the nearest market
The type of stock, the condition and age of the refrigeration plant, stand-by arrangements and whether power failure cover is included
The number of cold storage employees
e: Perishability of stock, plant reliability and stand-by power determine the likelihood and severity of deterioration.

t: A cold storage insures fruit under DOS with power failure extension. The electricity board cuts supply for 36 hours as scheduled load-shedding, and the stock deteriorates. The claim is:
o: Payable under the extension
Not payable, as deliberate withholding of supply/load-shedding by the authority is excluded
Payable at 50%
Payable only if a complaint was lodged with the electricity board
e: The extension covers accidental failure of supply; planned load-shedding, strikes and non-payment of dues are excluded.

t: Which of the following is correct regarding the sum insured under a CECR policy?
o: It should be the original construction cost
It should represent the current reinstatement value, or an agreed first-loss limit where total loss is improbable
It is always 10% of construction cost
It is the annual maintenance budget
e: CECR is usually arranged on reinstatement value; for very large linear assets first-loss limits are common.

t: The control level of solvency ratio that every insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Available solvency margin must be at least 150% of the required solvency margin; falling below triggers IRDAI action.

t: Which of the following is NOT a CECR subject matter?
o: Harbour jetty
Irrigation canal
Hydroelectric turbine
Railway embankment
e: The turbine is machinery and belongs under MBD; CECR covers civil structures only.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Under an ALOP policy the 'time excess' is usually expressed in:
o: Rupees
Percentage of the sum insured
Days or weeks of delay
Percentage of the project cost
e: The time excess is the number of days/weeks of delay borne by the insured before the indemnity period starts.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: An ALOP policy for a 500 MW power project has an indemnity period of 12 months, sum insured ₹240 crore (anticipated gross profit) and a time excess of 30 days. A turbine damaged during hot testing (covered under EAR) delays commercial operation by 120 days. Ignoring savings, the ALOP claim is approximately:
o: ₹80 crore
₹60 crore
₹59.2 crore
₹79 crore
e: Indemnifiable delay = 120 − 30 = 90 days; ₹240 crore ÷ 365 × 90 ≈ ₹59.2 crore.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Which statement about ALOP and the contractor is correct?
o: The contractor can insure his liquidated damages under ALOP
The contractor has no insurable interest in the principal's loss of profit and cannot take ALOP
The contractor must pay the ALOP premium under IRDAI rules
ALOP covers the contractor's idle plant hire charges
e: ALOP is a principal's cover; contractual penalties and idle plant are excluded from engineering policies.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Under MLOP, 'gross profit' is defined as:
o: Turnover less all expenses
Net profit plus insured standing charges
Net profit only
Sales less cost of raw materials only
e: As in fire LOP, gross profit comprises net trading profit and standing charges that continue despite reduced turnover.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 49% to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021; intermediaries may have 100%.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Which of the following reduces the amount payable under an MLOP claim?
o: Savings in standing charges that ceased or were reduced during the interruption
Increase in the sum insured
Shorter time excess
Reduced rate of gross profit declared
e: Savings in expenses during the interruption are deducted so that the insured is indemnified and not over-compensated.

t: A proposal is received for CAR on a bridge across a river in Assam to be built over 36 months. Which of the following would the underwriter consider most carefully?
o: The number of toll plazas
The contractor's GST registration
The colour of the bridge railing
Flood and earthquake exposure (seismic zone V) and the construction schedule relative to the monsoon
e: Assam is in zone V and prone to severe floods; AOG exposure and scheduling of the river works drive the rating and reinsurance.

t: Which document is the basic source of information for underwriting an engineering risk?
o: The proposal form and the specific questionnaire for the class of risk
The insurer's annual report
The IRDAI annual report
The contractor's newspaper advertisement
e: Proposal forms and questionnaires elicit the material facts; the underwriter supplements them with inspection and documents such as bar charts.

t: Which of the following is a typical factor increasing the CPM rate for a crane?
o: Use at a congested urban site with heavy lifts near existing structures
Use on a flat open site
A new machine with full maintenance contract
Operation by trained and certified operators
e: Site congestion and heavy lifts raise the accident potential; training and maintenance reduce it.

t: Under the Insurance Act, 1938, the provisions on surveyors and loss assessors are contained in Section:
o: 64VB
64UM
e: Section 64UM deals with licensing of surveyors and the requirement of survey reports; 64VB is premium in advance, 45 non-contestability and 41 rebating.

t: A surveyor's report on a CAR claim recommends ₹40 lakh. The insurer may:
o: Settle at a different amount only with recorded reasons, as the survey report is not binding but must be considered
Never deviate from the surveyor's figure
Ignore the report entirely
Ask the insured to appoint another surveyor
e: Under IRDAI regulations the surveyor's report is the basis of settlement but the insurer may, for recorded reasons, differ from it.
